standard_prerequisites.name: The maximal weakly etale subalgebra of an algebra over a field is weakly etale, is preserved by base change of the field, and is a field when the algebra is reduced and geometrically irreducible
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: invoked at proof lines 30988-30994 and again at proof lines 31064-31072
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the two sides of the comparison map and supplies the field structure used in the final computation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change of a weakly etale algebra along a field extension is weakly etale, which makes the comparison map injective
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the canonical injective map from the base changed subalgebra into the maximal subalgebra of the base changed algebra.

standard_prerequisites.name: The maximal weakly etale subalgebra is compatible with filtered colimits, so a statement about finite type algebras implies the general case
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the proof to the case of a finite type algebra over the base field.

standard_prerequisites.name: Weakly etale algebras over a field are reduced, which lets the nilpotent kernel of the reduction be discarded
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the comparison map stays injective when the algebra is replaced by its reduced quotient.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite separable extension of fields becomes a product of copies of the larger field after a base change to a separably closed or algebraically closed field
standard_prerequisites.use: Decomposes the tensor product of the algebra over the finite separable field with the algebraically closed field into a product of factors.

core_obligations: Set up the comparison map: the base change of the maximal weakly etale subalgebra of A is weakly etale over L and sits inside the base changed algebra, so there is a canonical injective map into the maximal weakly etale L-subalgebra of that algebra (proof lines 30988-30994).

Reduce to an algebraically closed base field by factoring through any extension: if the comparison is surjective after a further field extension then it was already surjective, so assume L algebraically closed (proof lines 30995-31001).
Reduce to a finite type algebra by writing A as the filtered colimit of its finite type subalgebras and using compatibility of the maximal subalgebra with filtered colimits (proof lines 31002-31006).

Reduce to a reduced algebra: the kernel of the reduction map is nilpotent, the maximal weakly etale L-subalgebra is reduced, and the maximal subalgebra of A over K equals that of its reduced quotient (proof lines 31007-31016).

In the reduced finite type case let K' be the maximal weakly etale subalgebra of A over K, which is a finite separable field extension of K, and note that A is geometrically irreducible over K' (proof lines 31064-31072).

Use that the tensor product of the finite separable extension with the algebraically closed field splits as a product of copies of that field, so the base changed algebra is a product of factors each geometrically irreducible over the large field, each having a unique minimal prime and maximal weakly etale subalgebra equal to that large field; decompose the subalgebras accordingly to get equality, and conclude by the permanence of weak etaleness (proof lines 31073-31101).
proof_roadmap: Build the canonical injective comparison map between the two candidate maximal subalgebras (proof lines 30988-30994).
Reduce to an algebraically closed base field and to a finite type algebra (proof lines 30995-31006).
Reduce further to a reduced algebra using the nilpotent kernel and reducedness of weakly etale algebras over a field (proof lines 31007-31016).
In that case decompose the base changed algebra along the finite separable field of constants and identify the maximal subalgebra of every factor (proof lines 31064-31097).
Conclude equality of the subalgebras on the product and finish with the permanence statement (proof lines 31098-31101).
